applies_why: The judge text marks Romans 1:3 UNDERDETERMINED because it lacks explicit textual resolution of paternity, which is the single-verse non-statement/openness the rule governs.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.
room: Phrase: 'does not state a link or its contrary.' Reading 1: a single verse's failure to state a link/contrary cannot make UNDERDETERMINED. Reading 2: such failure can make the verse open. The rule chooses Reading 1.
why: The judge expressly grounds UNDERDETERMINED on the absence of explicit textual resolution in the Romans 1:3 discussion, so it uses a single verse's non-statement/openness as the forbidden ground.
